sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
hindiTranslation: अर्जुन बोले  हे वार्ष्णेय  फिर यह मनुष्य न चाहता हुआ भी जबर्दस्ती लगाये हुएकी तरह किससे प्रेरित होकर पापका आचरण करता है ॥
englishTranslation: Arjuna said: O descendant of the Vrishni clan, what drives a person to commit wrongdoing, even unwillingly, as if forced?
essence: Compulsion has a cause, and Arjuna wants to name it.
speaker: Arjuna
simpleMeaning: Arjuna asks what makes a person do wrong even when they do not want to, as if some force is pushing them.
simpleInsight: It gives language to the strange moment when you feel split between intention and action.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna has already been told to rise above attachment and follow his duty. Instead of accepting the teaching, he turns to Krishna with a deeper question: what power makes people act against their own will?
modernRelevance: On Diwali night, a man who promised his wife he would skip the card game finds himself at the table again. Arjuna's question fits that night: what pushed him there against his own will?
translationLiteral: अर्जुन उवाच (Arjuna said) / अथ (then) / केन (by what) / प्रयुक्तः (impelled) / अयम् (this) / पापम् (wrongdoing) / चरति (does) / पूरुषः (person) / अनिच्छन् (not desiring) / अपि (even) / वार्ष्णेय (O descendant of the Vrishni clan) / बलात् (by force) / इव (as if) / नियोजितः (appointed / driven) ॥
insight: Arjuna asks what force drives a person to do wrong, even unwillingly, as if pushed.

quoteVariants.text: What force makes a person do wrong against their will?
Why do I do what I do not want?
